title: plugin-auth SCIM: a schema-refused request (400) from a valid connection is logged as `unknown` with no actor, so the SCIM console never shows the most common IdP push error
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, cloud `main` `de8d979` (framework pin `e24136c2`). Local SCIM run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3667. Follow-up to #31829 (closed).

## Measured
All requests below carried the **valid** bearer of connection `okta-test`:

| request | status | `sys_audit_log.actor` | `metadata.scim_connection_id` |
|---|---|---|---|
| duplicate `POST /Users` | 409 | `svc:scim:okta-test` | `okta-test` |
| `GET /Users/{unknown}` | 404 | `svc:scim:okta-test` | `okta-test` |
| `PATCH /Users/{id}` with op `explode` | 400 `invalidValue` | **null** | **`unknown`** (`presented_credential: scim_bearer`) |
| `POST /Users` with no `userName` | 400 `invalidValue` | **null** | **`unknown`** |

The cloud SCIM provisioning console filters on `actor starts_with 'svc:scim:'` (`SCIM_OPERATION_FILTER`). Both 400 rows are therefore invisible under the connection. They are the rows an administrator needs most when an IdP's attribute mapping is wrong: a mis-mapped Okta or Entra attribute surfaces as a schema 400 on every push.

## Why
This is the known vendor ordering, pinned in the header of `scim-refusal-audit.test.ts`: a body that fails the vendor's schema is refused **before** the bearer verifier runs, so `scimRequestScope` never gets `connectionId`. #31829's acceptance line ("the four refusals … each leave a row naming the connection (or 'unknown' for 401)") listed the malformed PATCH among the ones that should name the connection.

## Proposal
In `observeScimRefusal`, when the scope has no `connectionId` and the presented credential is a SCIM bearer, resolve it the way the verifier does (digest lookup in `sys_scim_connection_credential`, active and unexpired) before building the event. Only a credential that really resolves names a connection, so a forged bearer still reads `unknown`. The existing bound and secret rules stay as they are. Add a case to the suite: a schema 400 with a valid bearer names the connection.
